Title: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection in EncryptedXmlDecryptor
Analysis:
In `src/DataProtection/DataProtection/src/XmlEncryption/EncryptedXmlDecryptor.cs`, the `Decrypt` method receives an untrusted XML element (`encryptedElement` of type `XElement`) and loads it into an `XmlDocument` object using `xmlDocument.Load(new XElement(\"root\", encryptedElement).CreateReader())`. Since `XmlDocument` by default enables DTD processing/entity expansion or doesn't explicitly restrict external DTD resolution unless configured via `XmlReaderSettings`, parsing this user-supplied XML could lead to XML External Entity (XXE) injection or XML entity expansion (Billion Laughs) vulnerabilities. An attacker who can control or influence the XML passed to the `Decrypt` method could exploit this to read sensitive local files, perform SSRF, or trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) via resource exhaustion.

**Conceptual Exploit Payload:**
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE root [
  <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">
]>
<EncryptedData Type="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmlenc#Element" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmlenc#">
  <CipherData>
    <CipherValue>&xxe;</CipherValue>
  </CipherData>
</EncryptedData>
```
